ops.markdown:
**Wanderline** is a travel company; Farah is its CEO and founder. Carried over from last class.

**The business problem.** Enquiries arrive at three or four in the morning. Nobody acts on them. Clients are being lost.

An enquiry arriving at 3am does not need anyone's judgement at 3am — it needs someone to have seen it by 9am. That is what makes it automatable rather than a staffing problem.

**Why today looks different from last class.** Last class showed workflows but did not implement anything that responds to the client — a showcase, not a use case. Today is three iterated builds against one real scenario.

**Today's first goal**

> Whenever a new request comes in, consolidate it and email a summary to the team.

That sentence is Build 1's entire spec, and it reads straight onto the three-node starting rule: *whenever a new request comes in* is the input, *consolidate it* is the AI step, *email a summary* is somewhere to put the result.

Traps collected as they came up across the lecture.

**A workflow that is built but not published never triggers automatically.** Nothing errors and nothing is red — the canvas looks finished, the nodes are configured, testing works. To trigger automatically the workflow must be published and the publish button actually green.

ops.title: Build 1 — form to LLM chain to Gmail

ops.label: n8n Form trigger
ops.detail: Form title "Wanderline late-night inquiries", no authentication. Exposes a test URL and a production URL — sandbox for your own changes versus what clients see. Run Execute step and submit once, so the next node is configured against real sample data rather than guesses.

ops.label: Basic LLM Chain, with a Groq model sub-node
ops.detail: Source for prompt: define below, not the chat trigger. Prompt: "Summarize this travel inquiry in two short lines for our team inbox. In case of vague description you can clean and refine the text." The form's name and query are dragged in from the input panel, which converts each to an expression; the preview at the bottom shows the resolved prompt with the real values substituted.

ops.label: Gmail — send a message
ops.detail: To himself, subject "New request, please check", body = the chain's text output picked from the schema view, plus a sign-off. Credentials: OAuth every time when it is your own account; the API key route (enable the Gmail API in Google Cloud, create a project and key, free) is for when someone hands you a key for an account you are not logged into.

ops.label: It cannot tell a spam request from a real one
ops.detail: A query about grocery prices at the local market — nothing to do with travel — was summarised and emailed anyway. No spam detection means the inbox is overburdened and the person reading it drowns. The build is not broken: it does exactly what the goal sentence asked. The goal sentence was incomplete, and only a real submission showed that. This is what Build 2 answers.

cells.c-why: Someone will type +91 and a number field rejects it. Pick the field type by what people will actually enter, not by what the data nominally is
A text input caps out and silently truncates; a textarea expands and holds a long query. A travel enquiry is prose
Added mid-build after a student pointed out they were missing — the flow was already running when the gap surfaced
Nothing was mandatory on the first run: submitting with no email was accepted with no nudge. Set per element under Add an attribute

cells.c-verdict: Could be stable, but nowhere close to the frontier assistants
Would potentially work fine on a laptop through Ollama
Going to fail for sure on a laptop
Impossible even with two or three high-end NVIDIA cards
A simple request does not need an expensive model. Summarisation is simple — any model can do it

Check the cut-off date. A model with a 2023 cut-off is fine for English summarisation or general coding and useless on anything newer. There is no single reliable page for cut-offs — ask the model, or check the Ollama model pages
The small model picked here starts hallucinating in Build 3. "Simple task" is a judgement you can get wrong, and the symptom surfaces two builds later
Deliberately not recorded — every model name in the lecture is machine-heard and unverified. The thresholds are the lesson, not the labels

ops.markdown:
**Change the trigger, re-run the trigger.** Sample data is a snapshot of the last successful execution, not a live connection. Editing the form after submitting makes the earlier submission stale, and the node downstream summarises nothing.

**Drag the leaf, not the parent — and use schema view, not table view.** Schema view is the tree of an upstream node's output, so it is the only view where a branch and a leaf are distinguishable. Dragging a parent object produces `[object Object]` in the result.

**A node reporting success is not the outcome happening.** The Gmail node sent correctly and the mail was in Sent — it had landed in spam and was never received. n8n is telling the truth about its own node; delivery is somebody else's system.

**Revoking an OAuth grant silently breaks the workflow.** Every grant is visible and deletable under Overview → Credentials, but a workflow configured against a deleted credential stops working.
